clue.text: Like seat of milkmaid family in novelty contest

parts.note: a milking stool traditionally stands on three legs
a race is a family line or lineage

explanation.surface: A milkmaid's relatives turn up at a quirky country-show competition.
explanation.walkthrough: The milkmaid's seat is her milking stool, which classically has three legs so it stays steady on uneven ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Pairs tied together at the ankle stumble along in this comic sports-day event, so it is a novelty contest.

clue.text: Disturbed about Rugby Union, which is rewarding

indicators.note: one word goes round about the other, wrapping it on both sides

parts.note: fitful means restless, disturbed, as of sleep
the standard abbreviation of Rugby Union

explanation.surface: A troubled rugby union nonetheless turns out to be worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: Something productive that yields good results is fruitful, a close synonym of rewarding.

clue.text: Musical passage makes a doctor look up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looking up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written
doc is the informal word for a doctor; that these letters also run backwards through the printed words is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A piece of music is so stirring that a physician raises their eyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding section of a piece of music, a passage that rounds off a movement.

clue.text: Check comedian getting doubly hot and doddery

indicators.note: doubly says the hot letter appears twice

parts.note: a wit is a funny person, a comedian
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
doddery means shaky with age, so old

explanation.surface: A comic sweating under the lights and growing tottery with age.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or restrain it, the verb sense of withhold.

clue.text: Ne'er-do-well not wanted for breakfast!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an untrustworthy, worthless person
second meaning, taken literally: a rotten one from the hen

explanation.walkthrough: The second half is a playful literal reading of the idiom: nobody wants a rotten one fried for their morning meal.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a scoundrel, while literally it is a spoilt item of food nobody would eat at breakfast.

clue.text: I have to interrupt a scrap, having trembled

indicators.note: to interrupt something is to break into its middle, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a shred is a scrap or tiny piece
the contraction I've

explanation.surface: Someone who broke up a fight admits they were shaking afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To shiver is to shake or quiver, so having shivered is having trembled.

clue.text: It's able to be absorbed by dry lozenge

indicators.note: something absorbed is taken in and held inside another thing

parts.note: TT, teetotal, describes someone who stays off alcohol
taken as written

explanation.surface: A throat sweet that dissolves in a dry mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: Dry here means not drinking alcohol, and TT (teetotal) is the crossword's usual stand-in for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lozenge is a small medicinal sweet or pill, and a tablet is a compressed pill of the same kind.

clue.text: Moodily Paddy has the last word to work out

parts.note: a paddy is a fit of bad temper
amen is the final word of a prayer
to tally is to count up or reckon

explanation.surface: An irritable Irishman insists on having the final say in sorting a problem out.
explanation.walkthrough: Paddy looks like an Irish name, but a paddy is British slang for a tantrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting by temperament and mood swings, so temperamentally can describe behaving moodily or in an unpredictable way.

clue.text: Nearly listen to Lewinsky, a music maker

indicators.note: nearly means not quite all, so the final letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: hark is an old word for listen
Monica Lewinsky, the White House intern of the Clinton scandal

explanation.surface: Someone almost hears a famous intern, who has an instrument to play.
explanation.definitionFit: A harmonica is a small mouth organ, an instrument that produces music, so a music maker.

clue.text: Ending of "Paradise Lost" making one throw up

indicators.note: points at the final letter of the following word as the one affected
what is lost is gone, so that end letter is removed

parts.note: heaven is paradise

explanation.surface: The close of Milton's epic poem is so dreadful it makes a reader sick.
explanation.walkthrough: Paradise Lost looks like Milton's title, but it splits into the word and its deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to retch or gag, the body's effort to vomit, so it means throw up.

clue.text: Inscription reads "battered hat and broken pipe"

indicators.note: a broken pipe is in pieces, so its letters are mixed in with the hat's
a battered hat is knocked out of shape, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tombstone joke: the deceased left only a battered hat and a broken pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' and 'broken' each scramble their word, and the letters of HAT and PIPE mingle into one arrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: The words carved on a gravestone in memory of the dead are a form of inscription.

clue.text: Cloak love with pen somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters can be arranged freely

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A writer disguises romantic feelings in their writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To cloak something is to wrap or cover it completely, which is to envelop it.

clue.text: Biography contains untruth about female

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: a lie is an untruth
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: A book about a woman's life includes a falsehood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contains' looks like the container signal, but it only links the definition; 'about' does the wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: A biography is an account of someone's lifetime, often titled 'The Life of' its subject.

clue.text: Inhabitant of Tin Pay Alley?

parts.note: surface reading: a resident of some poorly paid back street; setter's reading: a play on Tin Pan Alley, the New York district of popular-music publishers, whose lyricists were often poorly paid

explanation.surface: Someone living in a shabby lane where wages are paltry.
explanation.walkthrough: Tin Pan Alley was the hub of American popular-music publishing; changing Pan to Pay hints at how little the tunesmiths earned.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers and lyricists of popular tunes worked in Tin Pan Alley, so its typical inhabitant writes music for a living.

clue.text: Virtuous knight had to follow the carnival

indicators.note: the word before must come after the one named next, fixing the order

parts.note: a gala is a festive carnival or celebration
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chaste Arthurian knight was obliged to trail behind a festival procession.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Galahad, the purest knight of the Round Table, is the byword for virtue and chastity.

clue.text: December 31: go climbing with a man in the hay

indicators.note: the earlier pieces are placed inside the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: taken as written
a man is simply a man; the article is part of the phrase

explanation.surface: A New Year's Eve tryst: a romp in the hay with a fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: Hogmanay is the Scottish name for New Year's Eve and its celebrations.
explanation.definitionFit: Scots celebrate the last night of the year as Hogmanay, so the date stands for the festival.

clue.text: Editor breaks brush in sleeping quarters

indicators.note: something that breaks into another lodges in its middle

parts.note: a broom is a long-handled brush
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor snaps a broom in the dormitory.
explanation.definitionFit: A bedroom is the room of a house where people sleep, its sleeping quarters.

clue.text: Old French prison to be shutting in a mute

indicators.note: shutting in means the two letters close round the following pieces

parts.note: taken as the word be, with to linking
still can mean silent or mute

explanation.surface: A grim old French jail is set to lock up someone who cannot speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' only links; 'a mute' splits as the article plus an adjective, and 'still' as silent is the sense needed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the Paris fortress-jail stormed in 1789 at the start of the Revolution.

clue.text: Frank to kiss with collar unbuttoned

parts.note: frank means candid, open
to neck is to kiss and cuddle

explanation.surface: Someone called Frank sets out for a smooch, shirt casually undone.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name, but here it is the adjective meaning candid.
explanation.definitionFit: An open-neck shirt is worn without a tie and with the top button undone, leaving the collar open.

clue.text: Matthew, Mark, Luke or John?

parts.note: surface reading: four ordinary men's first names, perhaps a choice of name for a baby; setter's reading: the four writers to whom the New Testament gospels are attributed

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that any one of the four names is meant as an example of the class.
explanation.definitionFit: Each of the four gospel writers is known by the title of the class of authors the clue points to.

clue.text: Get-together with a very loud tune

parts.note: taken as written
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud
an air is a tune or melody

explanation.surface: A party where a song is blasting out at top volume.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair can be a social event or occasion, such as a party, so a get-together.

clue.text: Kind of bean might make ten ill

indicators.note: suggests the letters could be made into something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dodgy batch of pulses could make a whole group of people sick.
explanation.definitionFit: The lentil is a small edible pulse, a legume loosely counted among the beans.

clue.text: Penny-pinching plan

explanation.walkthrough: Together the words read like a scheme for saving money; separately they are two senses of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective the word means stingy with money; as a verb it means to intend or have in mind.

clue.text: Hold back referee and rain will follow

indicators.note: the second piece comes after the first, fixing their order

parts.note: ref is short for referee
taken as written

explanation.surface: A match official is told to delay because a downpour is coming.
explanation.definitionFit: To refrain is to restrain yourself from doing something, to abstain or desist.

clue.text: Iberian princess ain't moving when holding fan

indicators.note: holding something means having it inside, so the rearranged letters surround the other word
letters that are moving shift about into a new order

parts.note: the contraction, apostrophe dropped
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Spanish royal stays perfectly still while clutching her fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is a daughter of the king of Spain or Portugal, the two Iberian monarchies.

clue.text: Cigarettes for young public school "slaves"

definitions.meaning: first meaning: British slang for cigarettes
second meaning: junior boys who once had to run errands for senior pupils

explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a public school is a private fee-paying school, where the old fagging system made younger boys servants to older ones.
explanation.definitionFit: The British slang word for cigarettes is also the old name for junior pupils who served seniors at boarding schools.

clue.text: Mate hidden by ostrich in Africa

indicators.note: the letters sit concealed within the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of the first word, all of the second and the start of the third

explanation.surface: A friend is concealed by a big bird on the savannah.
explanation.walkthrough: China plate is cockney rhyming slang for mate, shortened as usual to its first word.
explanation.definitionFit: In rhyming slang 'china plate' rhymes with mate, so china means a friend or pal.

clue.text: Gallic oil could be unsound

indicators.note: suggests the letters could be turned into something else when rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: French olive oil might be of poor quality.
explanation.definitionFit: An unsound argument is one with faulty reasoning, which is what illogical describes.
